overview:
Maryland's second district leans Democratic by about ten points, and first-term incumbent Johnny Olszewski enters the general election with the advantages that typically come with the seat. He has raised roughly 1.2 million dollars and holds 644,000 dollars on hand, while Republican Dave Wallace has raised about 20,000 dollars and reports just over 3,000 dollars in the bank. No outside groups have spent against Olszewski, and no public polling of the race is available.

Without surveys, the forecast rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and the lopsided money race, all of which point comfortably to Olszewski. Betting markets put his chances in the mid-nineties. The seat has stayed in Democratic hands for decades, and nothing in the fundraising record suggests Wallace can force a competitive contest. A surprise would require a dramatic late shift in the national environment.
